senses.sense_definition: A synthetic surface resembling natural grass, used mainly for sports fields and lawns.

examples.text: The local stadium replaced its worn grass field with durable green <w>astroturf</w>.
They decided to lay <w>astroturf</w> across the small backyard to reduce lawn maintenance.

senses.sense_definition: A campaign or movement artificially created by a political or corporate entity to simulate spontaneous public support.

examples.text: The protest looked genuine at first, but critics soon exposed it as corporate <w>astroturf</w>.
Journalists investigated the funding behind the sudden campaign and uncovered an orchestrated <w>astroturf</w>.

senses.sense_definition: To cover a surface or area with synthetic grass.

examples.text: The homeowner decided to <w>astroturf</w> the patio so the pets would have a soft area to play.
The school wanted to <w>astroturf</w> the outdoor sports ground before the upcoming tournament.

senses.sense_definition: To manufacture a misleading appearance of widespread grassroots or public support for a particular agenda.

examples.text: A lobbying firm was hired to <w>astroturf</w> support for the controversial energy policy.
They used automated accounts on social media to <w>astroturf</w> widespread backing for their client.

senses.sense_definition: Created or funded by a corporation or political group while masquerading as a spontaneous, grassroots initiative.

examples.text: The committee realized that the flood of messages was driven by an <w>astroturf</w> campaign.
Several corporate sponsors funded <w>astroturf</w> groups to sway public opinion against the regulation.
